chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Talha ibn Zayd, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who acts without insight is like the traveller upon a road other than the right one — the speed of his travel increases him nothing but distance.'

key_terms.السائر على غير الطريق: Travelling not on the road — the analogy for misguided action
key_terms.العامل: Al-'amil — the one who acts, the practitioner; here implying religious practice
key_terms.بصيرة: Basira — inner insight, religious discernment, knowledge that guides action

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about acting without knowledge or insight?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) uses a vivid analogy to warn against acting without proper religious knowledge and discernment. Just as a traveller on the wrong road only gets further from his destination the faster he moves, a person who performs religious deeds without grounded understanding only strays further from the truth. This hadith was likely addressed to those who engaged in worship or practice zealously but without sound guidance, a concern deeply relevant in the early Islamic period when competing religious trends proliferated.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from Talha Bin Zayd who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who acts upon without an insight is like the traveller upon another road. The quickness of the travel would not increase him except for the distance (from his destination)’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Talha ibn Zayd who has said the following. “
(Imam) abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) has said, ‘Working without understanding and insight is like travelling in the wrong direction that only takes one farther away from the destination.’”
